cards.explanation: The answer is “Follow Me.” Two words. That's the whole invitation: “Follow Me,” He told him. No speech, no list of rules, just a call to a man at a tax booth, friends. And Matthew got up and followed Him.

The answer is many tax collectors and sinners. That's the guest list at Matthew's house, friends. They came and ate with Jesus and His disciples. Matthew was a tax collector himself, so I think his contacts list was heavy on that crowd. The table was full.

The answer is False. The question goes to the disciples. The Pharisees asked His disciples, “Why does your Teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?” The text doesn't say they asked Jesus. Then, on hearing this, Jesus answers.

The answer is sick, friends. Jesus says, “It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick.” It's an easy picture. Somebody who's hurting is the one heading for the doctor's office. The sick are the ones who need the doctor.

The answer is sinners. Jesus says, “For I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners.” That's His answer to the Pharisees about who He's eating with, friends. The people at Matthew's table are the very ones He came to call.

The answer is False. It's flipped, friends. John's disciples ask, “Why is it that we and the Pharisees fast so often, but Your disciples do not fast?” They and the Pharisees fast often, and Jesus's disciples don't. Their question is about that difference.

The answer is the time the bridegroom is taken from them. Jesus says, “But the time will come when the bridegroom will be taken from them; then they will fast.” Think about it, friends: nobody shows up to a wedding with a long face while the groom is standing right there. The mourning waits until He's taken from them. So the fasting isn't about a rule, it's about who is in the room.

The answer is that the patch pulls away and the tear gets worse. Jesus says, “For the patch will pull away from the garment, and a worse tear will result.” The patch He means is unshrunk cloth sewn on an old garment, friends. So the fix makes the problem bigger. The hole ends up worse than before.

The answer is True. Jesus says it plainly: if men pour new wine into old wineskins, “…the skins will burst, the wine will spill, and the wineskins will be ruined.” Everything goes wrong at once, friends. It's one bad pour with three bad endings.

The answer is that the wine and the skins are both kept safe. Jesus says, “Instead, they pour new wine into new wineskins, and both are preserved.” Both the wine and the skins come through fine, friends. When the new goes into new, nothing gets lost.
